- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

</system-reminder>

content.content:
model Node {
  id               String        @id @default(cuid())
  name             String        @unique
  pveNode          String // Proxmox node name (e.g. ns5002569)
  apiUrl           String // https://host:8006
  tokenId          String
  tokenSecret      String
  publicIp         String
  bridge           String        @default("vmbr1")
  subnetPrefix     String        @default("10.20.0.") // /24 NAT subnet prefix
  ipStart          Int           @default(100)
  ipEnd            Int           @default(250)
  sshPortStart     Int           @default(20000)
  sshPortEnd       Int           @default(29999)
  natChain         String        @default("NXEON_FWD")
  storageNvme      String        @default("vmdata")
  storageHdd       String        @default("vmdata-hdd")
  capacityRamMB    Int           @default(56000)
  // What the platform actually PAYS the infra provider (OVH/Hetzner/etc) to
  // rent this physical box each month — admin-entered, not derived from
  // anything else. Null (not 0) until an operator fills it in: a real node
  // is never free, so 0 would misreport "unconfigured" as "no cost". Purely
  // a cost/margin-visibility figure for /admin/nodes — never read by the
  // scheduler or billing engine.
  monthlyCostCents Int?
  isPrimary        Boolean       @default(false)
  enabled          Boolean       @default(true)
  status           NodeStatus    @default(ONLINE)
  provider         NodeProvider  @default(OVH)
  // Provider's own datacenter code (e.g. "sgp1", "fsn1") — a plain validated
  // string, not an enum: see lib/node-regions.ts's NODE_REGIONS/REGION_LABELS
  // for the same "fast-changing categorical value, validated in code not the
  // DB" convention this schema already uses for StaffGrant.area.
  region           String        @default("sgp1")
  // The provider's OWN identifier for this physical box — OVH's "service
  // name" (e.g. "ns5002569.ip-51-79-162.net") or Hetzner's server number
  // (e.g. "2769362") — distinct from `pveNode` (Proxmox's own node name) and
  // `apiUrl`/`tokenId`/`tokenSecret` (the Proxmox API credentials). Needed by
  // lib/dedicated-ip.ts's per-node provider branch to make the right
  // OVH/Hetzner REST calls for THIS node's IP pool specifically. Nullable —
  // only required for a node that actually pools dedicated IPs.
  providerServerId String?
  // Node-agent (Class-B fixes: NAT sync, cloud-init snippet write, dnat-check —
  // see docs/DOCUMENTATION.md's "Multi-node synergy" for the full design). The
  // agent is the CALLEE; the worker on the primary is the CALLER, so unlike
  // Server.rootPasswordEnc's peers this must be DECRYPTABLE, not hashed — the
  // primary has to actually present the token on every request, the same
  // direction as `tokenSecret` above (also plaintext) but encrypted at rest
  // via lib/crypto-box.ts, since AUTH_SECRET-derived encryption was already
  // the established pattern for "a secret the app must read back" (rootPasswordEnc,
  // sourcePasswordEnc, anthropicKeyEnc) and tokenSecret predates it. Null on
  // the primary (which never runs the agent) and on any node onboarded before
  // Phase 3 shipped, until it's rotated in.
  agentTokenEnc    String?
  // Port the agent listens on for this node. A field, not a hardcoded
  // constant, so a node whose default port is already taken can be onboarded
  // without a code change.
  agentPort        Int           @default(8943)
  lastSeenAt       DateTime?
  createdAt        DateTime      @default(now())
  servers          Server[]
  dedicatedIps     DedicatedIp[]

  // Distinct from `enabled` — a disabled node drops off scheduling AND out of
  // most admin surfaces (it's meant for a node that's genuinely gone/retired).
  // This is narrower: "keep this node fully visible and its existing servers
  // running, just stop landing NEW provisions on it" — e.g. a node running
  // hot that shouldn't take more load without being torn out of the fleet.
  // Read by lib/node-capacity.ts scheduleNode(); the admin Infrastructure page
  // toggles it directly. Default true so every existing node behaves exactly
  // as before this field existed.
  acceptsProvisions Boolean       @default(true)
}

# Save payment details during payment

Learn how to accept a payment and save your customer's payment details for future purchases.

Read this page in your terminal: [install the Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/install) (v1.43.3+) and run `stripe docs`. [Reference](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/docs)

## Start here: Integrate with Stripe using skills and plugins

Stripe provides skills and plugins for agents to build faster and more accurately. See [Agent skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md) for more information.

**Quickstart**: Install the Stripe CLI with `npm install -g @stripe/cli` and run `stripe agent setup`.

# Embedded form


> Learn more about [the embedded form integration](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/how-checkout-works.md?payment-ui=checkout-form).

Use the [Checkout Sessions API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions.md) with the embedded form to save payment details during a purchase.

There are also some payment method restrictions to be aware of when saving payment methods with the embedded form.

> When using the embedded form, only cards are supported for saved payment methods. You can’t save other payment methods, such as bank accounts.

## Prerequisites

1. Follow the Checkout guide to [accept a payment](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/accept-a-payment.md?payment-ui=checkout-form).
2. Follow this guide to save the payment method used during a payment so you can retrieve it for use in future payments by the same customer.

## Enable saved payment methods

> Global privacy laws are complicated and nuanced. Before implementing the ability to store customer payment method details, work with your legal team to make sure that it complies with your privacy and compliance framework.

To allow a customer to save their payment method for future use, specify the [saved_payment_method_options.payment_method_save](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md#create_checkout_session-saved_payment_method_options-payment_method_save) parameter when creating the Checkout Session.

Saving a payment method requires a customer. This can be either a customer-configured [Account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md#v2_account_object-configuration-customer) object or [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object.md) object. Pass an existing customer or create a new one by setting [customer_creation](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md#create_checkout_session-customer_creation) to `always` on the Checkout Session.

> #### Use the Accounts v2 API to represent customers
> 
> The Accounts v2 API is generally available for Connect users, and in public preview for other Stripe users. If you’re part of the Accounts v2 preview, you need to specify a [preview version](https://docs.stripe.com/api-v2-overview.md#sdk-and-api-versioning) in your code.
> 
> To join the Accounts v2 preview, go to [Account previews and features](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/previews) in your Dashboard and enable **Reusable payment methods for Global Payouts**.
> 
> For most use cases, we recommend [modelling your customers as customer-configured Account objects](https://docs.stripe.com/accounts-v2/use-accounts-as-customers.md) instead of using [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers.md) objects.

```curl
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/checkout/sessions \
  -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
  -d "line_items[0][price]={{PRICE_ID}}" \
  -d "line_items[0][quantity]=2" \
  -d mode=payment \
  -d ui_mode=form \
  -d customer_creation=always \
  -d "saved_payment_method_options[payment_method_save]=enabled"
```

After you create the Checkout Session, use the [client secret](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/object.md#checkout_session_object-client_secret) returned in the response to [build your checkout page](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/quickstart.md).

## Re-use a previously saved payment method

Each saved payment method is linked to a customer, either as customer-configured [Account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md#v2_account_object-configuration-customer) object or a [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object.md) object. Before creating the Checkout Session, authenticate your customer and pass their ID to the Checkout Session.

The embedded form automatically redisplays previously saved payment methods for your customer to use during checkout when saved payment methods are enabled on the Checkout Session.

#### Accounts v2

```curl
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/checkout/sessions \
  -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
  -d "line_items[0][price]={{PRICE_ID}}" \
  -d "line_items[0][quantity]=2" \
  -d mode=payment \
  -d ui_mode=form \
  -d "customer_account={{CUSTOMERACCOUNT_ID}}"
```

#### Customers v1

```curl
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/checkout/sessions \
  -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
  -d "line_items[0][price]={{PRICE_ID}}" \
  -d "line_items[0][quantity]=2" \
  -d mode=payment \
  -d ui_mode=form \
  -d "customer={{CUSTOMER_ID}}"
```

# Updates default behaviour for saved payment methods in Elements with Checkout Sessions

Read this page in your terminal: [install the Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/install) (v1.43.3+) and run `stripe docs`. [Reference](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/docs)

## Start here: Integrate with Stripe using skills and plugins

Stripe provides skills and plugins for agents to build faster and more accurately. See [Agent skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md) for more information.

**Quickstart**: Install the Stripe CLI with `npm install -g @stripe/cli` and run `stripe agent setup`.

## What’s new

Updates Elements with Checkout Sessions to automatically enable saved payment method collection and redisplay the saved payment methods in the Payment Element by default. This change means you don’t need to explicitly configure these options in your client-side integration when [a customer ID is passed to the Checkout Session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2025-09-30.clover#create_checkout_session-customer) (for redisplay) or when [saved_payment_method_options.payment_method_save](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2025-09-30.clover#create_checkout_session-saved_payment_method_options-payment_method_save) is enabled (for collection).

## Why is this a breaking change?

Previously, to enable saved payment methods with Elements and Checkout Sessions, you had to configure saved payment methods both on the Checkout Session and explicitly in your client-side `initCheckout()` call. Now, when you enable saved payment methods on the Checkout Session, the Payment Element automatically enables collection and redisplay without requiring additional client-side configuration. This changes the default behaviour for integrations that enabled saved payment methods on the Checkout Session but intentionally omitted the client-side configuration – those integrations will now have saved payment method collection and redisplay enabled automatically.

## Impact

You can now integrate saved payment methods in Elements with Checkout Sessions with simplified client-side configuration. Previously, you had to enable saved payment methods both on the Checkout Session and explicitly in your `initCheckout()` call. Now, when you enable saved payment methods on the Checkout Session, the Payment Element automatically enables collection and redisplay of saved payment methods without requiring additional client-side configuration.

This reduces integration complexity and ensures consistent saved payment method behaviour across your Elements with Checkout Sessions implementation. If you want to disable saved payment methods, you can still explicitly set `enableSave` and `enableRedisplay` to `never` in your [elementsOptions.savedPaymentMethod](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/init#custom_checkout_init-options-elementsOptions-savedPaymentMethod) configuration.

## Related changes

- [Prevents reusing client secrets for Intents in certain states when initialising Elements](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/clover/2025-09-30/client-secret-reuse.md)
- [Removes deprecated messaging and bank elements that were replaced](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/clover/2025-09-30/stripejs-deprecated-elements-removal.md)

content.thinking:
Subtracting TLS from TTFB gives server processing around 5ms, but the connect time of 7-16ms from this box to itself seems odd, possibly a hairpin through OVH's network. That puts RTT around 10-20ms, yet the browser's 53ms median suggests connections weren't being reused—each no-cors request may be triggering a fresh TLS handshake, since omitting credentials pushes Chrome into a separate anonymous socket pool.

I'm wondering if nginx's HTTP/2 support should allow reuse, but maybe a `Connection: close` header or something else is forcing fresh handshakes each time. Since cross-origin timing data is restricted without Timing-Allow-Origin, I think the best path is to test directly in Playwright by running several sequential no-cors fetches to the target and timing them myself.

## How to read the change history

```
 Part VII is ordered oldest → newest in three layers:
   1. "Change history — the first 28 commits"   the compressed early record
   2. dated / titled entries                    one H2 per shipped change
   3. "Session log — 2026-07-26/27"             the most recent waves

```

  then $X/mo" — replacing the mint "FREE FIRST MONTH" tag. Email has no intro pricing and is unchanged. The

  formats through `useMoney()` (display currency) instead of catalog's hard-coded-USD `money()`. The service tile's
  "First month free" pill on Cloud Hosting is a service tile, not a plan card, and was left as is.

  (`components/nx/useRegionLatency.ts`): once the region step is on screen, each region with a probe URL gets one
  warm-up request, then 5 timed `no-store` requests (sequential, `no-cors` + no credentials when cross-origin); the card
  shows the **median**. No probe or all samples failed → a neutral "— ms", never an estimate (`Region.ms` in
  `lib/nx/catalog.ts` is still nominal and still never printed). Probe URLs come from `lib/region-probe.ts`:
  `REGION_PROBE_URLS="sgp1=/api/tools/ping,fsn1=https://…"` (same-origin path or `https://` only), defaulting to the
  app's own `/api/tools/ping` for the **primary node's** region (the portal is served from the primary). **fsn1 has no
  browser-reachable endpoint today** (node-2 exposes only Proxmox/node-agent on self-signed certs and NAT'd game/VM
  ports), so Falkenstein shows "— ms" until a tiny static file is served over valid HTTPS from node-2 and added to
  `REGION_PROBE_URLS`.
- **Payment: "Use a different card".** `components/nx/NxCardFields.tsx` reads the Checkout Session's own
  `savedPaymentMethods` and shows them as a chooser ("Visa •••• 0077 · Saved card · expires 12/34" / "Use a different
  card"). The saved card is pre-selected and confirms with `checkout.confirm({ paymentMethod })`; "Use a different
  card" mounts the Payment Element blank and confirms it as before. The Elements provider now sets

  session still reports them). Same session, same `/api/stripe/confirm` return, same fulfilment — the card that paid is
  still recorded by `saveCardFromPaymentSession` (`card.saved (via payment)`); no card/audit writes were added. Verified
  in Stripe **test mode** (dev harness): saved-card payment and new-card (Mastercard 4444) payment both `paid`/
  `succeeded`. Note: Stripe only redisplays cards saved through Checkout with `allow_redisplay: always`.
- **Pay button** uses the portal's standard deploy CTA `.btn-deploy` (+ `.dep-arrow`) instead of the one-off
  cyan→pink `.btn-pay`; labels, loading/disabled states unchanged, disabled buttons no longer lift/shimmer on hover.
  `.btn-pay` in `app/globals.css` is now unused.

**Files:** `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`, `components/nx/{OrderBits,DeployView,NxCardFields,order-types,useRegionLatency}.ts(x)`,
`lib/region-probe.ts`, `lib/nx/catalog.ts`.
'''
assert anchor in s

input.message:
All four changes are in, committed on `feat/deploy-wizard-tweaks` as commit `28afe4e0a1`. Worktree: `/root/nxeon-worktrees/deploy-wizard-tweaks`. It's a local commit only: the post-commit hook did not push it and `origin/feat/deploy-wizard-tweaks` doesn't exist. I did not touch staging or prod, and nothing is promoted.

There was no usable login, so I checked the wizard with a dev-only copy of the deploy page (no auth, staging DB read-only). Playwright answered the auth-gated server actions with real `orderQuote`/`gameOrderQuote` results and real test-mode Stripe sessions. The harness files and the dev-only env var are deleted, the dev server on 3040 is stopped, and the test Stripe customer is deleted. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes.

**1. Discount badges removed (VPS, game, hosting, email)**
- The orange "🔥 X% OFF · FIRST …" pill is gone from VPS plan cards and game tier cards. The big price is now the intro price, with a small plain line under it: "First month, then $X/mo" ("First term, …" on longer terms). The Order summary's "Renews at …" line is unchanged.
- **Hosting:** its first-month-free offer had a mint "FREE FIRST MONTH" tag. It now follows the same pattern: `$0/mo` with "First month, then $X/mo" underneath. This only shows for customers still eligible for the offer.
- **Email:** has no intro pricing, so nothing changed there.
- **Leftovers removed:** the unused `introPercent` field and `introBadgePercent()`.
- **Two small fixes I made along the way:**
  - The VPS intro price now goes through `planIntroMonthlyCents` instead of the raw column, so a bad intro value can't be shown as the headline.
  - The VPS plan card now uses the currency-aware formatter (`useMoney()`); it was the one card still hard-coded to USD.
- **Left alone:** the term selector, and the "First month free" pill on the Cloud Hosting *service tile*, since that's not a plan card.
- **Staging has no intro prices at all.** To see the intro state, the harness used production's real values (read-only), e.g. Starter $12.78 → $8.88.

**2. Region latency: real in Singapore only**
- **How it's measured:** the visitor's browser times real round trips once the region step is on screen: one warm-up request, then 5 timed requests one after another, and the card shows the median.
- **What the card shows:**
  - Measured: "Asia · 53 ms".
  - Still running: a subtle "measuring…" that doesn't animate under reduced motion.
  - No endpoint for that region: a neutral "— ms", never an estimate.
- **Singapore is real:** it's measured against the app's existing `/api/tools/ping`. The portal is served from the primary node, which is in Singapore. From this box I saw 44–68 ms, which is the box reaching its own public IP.
- **Falkenstein (node-2) has no endpoint a browser can reach**, so it shows "— ms". Node-2 only exposes Proxmox and the node agent on self-signed certificates, plus NAT'd game/VM ports; its port 443 isn't TLS.
- **Smallest fix:** serve a tiny static file from node-2 over HTTPS with a valid certificate (e.g. a `fsn1` hostname with a `no-store` header). Then set `REGION_PROBE_URLS="sgp1=/api/tools/ping,fsn1=https://<host>/ping"` in `.env`. No CORS headers are needed and no code change.
- **Staging will show "— ms" in both regions**, because the staging DB has no primary node.

**3. Payment: "Use a different card"**
- The card area now lists the customer's saved cards from the Stripe session ("Visa •••• 0077 · Saved card · expires 12/34"), with "Use a different card" below.
- The saved card is pre-selected. Choosing "Use a different card" opens the existing blank Stripe card form.
- I turned off Stripe's own saved-card list inside that form so the card isn't shown twice; the session still reports the saved cards.
- It uses the same session, return page and fulfilment as before. The card that paid is still recorded the existing way (`card.saved (via payment)`); I added no card or audit writes.
- Staging's Stripe keys are **test keys**. End-to-end test-mode payments both succeeded: one with the saved card, one with a new Mastercard (…4444) entered via "Use a different card".
- In testing, Stripe only re-offered a card that had been saved through a checkout; a card attached directly via the API didn't appear.

**4. Pay button**
- It now uses `.btn-deploy`, the same class as the dashboard's "Deploy your first service" button, instead of the cyan→pink `.btn-pay`. Labels, loading/disabled states and reduced-motion behaviour are unchanged, and a disabled button no longer lifts or shimmers on hover.
- `.btn-pay` in `app/globals.css` is now unused; I left it in place.

**Files changed:**
- `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`
- `components/nx/OrderBits.tsx`
- `components/nx/DeployView.tsx`
- `components/nx/NxCardFields.tsx`
- `components/nx/order-types.ts`
- `components/nx/useRegionLatency.ts` (new)
- `lib/region-probe.ts` (new)
- `lib/nx/catalog.ts`
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` (new dated entry at the end)

**Screenshots** are in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/deploy-wizard-tweaks-shots/` (20 files):
- Plan, region and payment steps: `vps-1-plan`, `vps-2-region`, `vps-3-payment`, and the same three for `game-`.
- Hosting and email: `hosting-1-plan-promo`, `hosting-1-plan-nopromo`, `hosting-3-payment`, `email-1-plan`, `email-3-payment`.
- Mobile (390px): `mobile-vps-1-plan`, `mobile-vps-2-region`, `mobile-vps-3-payment`.
- Card chooser and payments: `card-after`, `e2e-saved-a`, `e2e-newcard-a/b/c`, `card-light-newcard` (light theme).

**Not verified:**
- The real signed-in page, including the real `payAndDeploy` and `/api/stripe/confirm` fulfilment, since the server actions were stood in for.
- Behaviour with live Stripe keys.
- Real production latency from a customer's location.
- The screenshots' order summaries show staging prices while the cards show production intro prices; that mismatch is only from the harness.

**Left for you:**
1. Get node-2 a small HTTPS ping file and set `REGION_PROBE_URLS` (above) so Falkenstein shows a real number.
2. Decide whether the "First month free" pill on the Cloud Hosting service tile should go too.
3. A pre-existing wording issue I noticed: when a hosting order is fully covered by the free month, the payment panel says "Covered by your balance", even with a $0 balance.
